It already solves every KNOWN vuln class, so run it FIRST (`.venv/bin/python solve.py --contract <contract.json> --artifacts <dir>`) and confirm. Do NOT rewrite it. ONLY if /api/clues shows a brand-new clue key the dispatch does not recognise: submit the proof first, then WEB CLASS LOGIC GOES IN A PLUGIN: `lib/web/handlers/day31_web_full_stack_incident.py` -- (1) write the draft `$TMPDIR/day31_web_full_stack_incident.py`: `KEY_MAP = [(r"<regex on a /api/clues KEY>", "day31_web_full_stack_incident")]`, `HANDLERS = {"day31_web_full_stack_incident": exploit}`, `def exploit(base, clues) -> "proof_..." or None` re-running the exploit end to end (recon what is per-target, then exploit, then read the proof; `lib.websolve.fetch` / `PROOF_RE`, short timeouts, browser UA, nothing from your shell session); (2) run `.venv/bin/python -m lib.web.plugin $TMPDIR/day31_web_full_stack_incident.py <a live target url from the contract's targets[]>` -- it imports the draft, checks its KEY_MAP dispatches on that target's /api/clues, runs it, prints `PROOF proof_...` and PROMOTES it to `lib/web/handlers/day31_web_full_stack_incident.py` (atomic; exit 1 = no proof, 2 = not a plugin, 3 = KEY_MAP matches no clue key: fix the draft and re-run). Never write that path directly. lib.web.handlers auto-loads it. Never edit solve.py's dispatch or lib/web/handlers/__init__.py (two web chains may run at once). Key on a concept clue KEY -- never on proof-N or a target slot: Mastery puts today's class on ANY of its 3 targets. (The answer-first worker usually promotes it before CORRECT; a codify worker hardens it after.)
